headline: Contracts source-verified on Etherscan with multiple recognized-firm audits, but all audits are >3 years stale, ChainSecurity flagged deployment-vs-audited-commit mismatch, and no pinned commit SHA could be confirmed this run.

findings.text: RootChainManager proxy (0xa0c68c638235ee32657e8f720a23cec1bfc77c77) and its implementation (0xf0235dca8fb0d3999685724dcbb9dd00c5d62dfa, labelled RootChainManager) are both tagged as source-verified on Etherscan (submitted 2020-08-26, Solidity 0.6.6, EIP-897 DelegateProxy pattern). ERC20 Bridge proxy (0x40ec5b33f54e0e8a33a975908c5ba1c14e5bbbdf) and its implementation (0x1f4c1e0afbeb5b5b86d7722549274434b29884f6, labelled ERC20Predicate) are also shown as source-verified on Etherscan with the same submission. Direct Etherscan page fetches were blocked; evidence derives from search-result page snippets that display the verified source and implementation ABI labels.

Public GitHub repo https://github.com/maticnetwork/pos-portal is the canonical source for the PoS bridge contracts (Solidity 77.1%, 735 commits, GPL-3.0). The repo structure (contracts/, audits/, migrations/) corresponds to the Etherscan-visible contract code. No commit SHA was pinned this run because the Etherscan page fetch was blocked — recorded in unknowns.

The README of the repo lists four audits: Hexens (PDF in repo), Halborn (PDF dated 2021-07-07), CertiK (PDF), PeckShield (PDF dated 2021-07-30). A fifth audit by ChainSecurity is documented at https://www.chainsecurity.com/security-audit/polygon-pos-portal-smart-contracts (fetched this run). All known audit dates are 2021, making them >3.5 years old as of analysis date 2026-05-07. No follow-up or differential audit covering the post-2021 deployment state was found. ChainSecurity's report explicitly states: 'This review covered a system already deployed. The actual contracts deployed do not exactly correspond to the version audited, although the changes are mostly of cosmetic nature only. The compiler version + dependencies used are outdated, however no known bug affects the live contracts.'

Auditing firms confirmed: Halborn (broadly recognized), PeckShield (broadly recognized), CertiK (broadly recognized), Hexens (recognized), ChainSecurity (broadly recognized — listed in the prompt's recognized-firm set). All five firms are recognized in Solidity audit context. No unknown-only auditor concern applies.

ChainSecurity's report (fetched 2026-05-07) explicitly notes the deployed contracts do not exactly correspond to the audited version, characterizing changes as 'mostly of cosmetic nature only' with no known bug affecting live contracts. However, the report also notes 'The compiler version + dependencies used are outdated.' No sampled diff of the content changes was possible in this run (direct Etherscan and GitHub commit-diff fetches blocked); quantifying whether changes are truly cosmetic cannot be independently confirmed. The audit itself was conducted on an already-deployed system in a retrospective capacity. Recorded as orange-weight drift uncertainty.

Both the RootChainManager proxy and its implementation are listed by Etherscan as separately verified (implementation label 'RootChainManager' at 0xf0235dca8fb0d3999685724dcbb9dd00c5d62dfa; ERC20 Bridge implementation 'ERC20Predicate' at 0x1f4c1e0afbeb5b5b86d7722549274434b29884f6). The EIP-897 DelegateProxy pattern is a recognized proxy standard and its 'Similar Match' status does not constitute a verification gap per the slice rules.

steelman.red: Direct on-chain Etherscan fetches were blocked and no commit SHA was pinned, so bytecode verification cannot be positively confirmed from fetched artifacts alone — and all audits are >3.5 years stale with an explicit auditor acknowledgment that deployed code deviates from the audited commit.
steelman.orange: Source-verified proxy + implementation pairs exist on Etherscan (confirmed via search-result page snippets), a public repo is accessible at maticnetwork/pos-portal with matching contract structure, and five recognized auditing firms have reviewed the codebase — but every known audit predates 2026 by more than 3.5 years, ChainSecurity flagged a deployment-vs-audit-commit mismatch, and no differential or follow-up audit was found for the post-2021 period.
steelman.green: The PoS bridge is one of the most widely-used Ethereum↔Polygon bridges, has been audited by five recognized firms including ChainSecurity, has consistently verified source on Etherscan since 2020, holds a public GPL-3.0 repo, and ChainSecurity characterized any post-audit changes as 'mostly cosmetic' with no known bug affecting live contracts.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because: while multiple recognized auditors reviewed the code and the contracts appear source-verified, every known audit is 2021-vintage (>3.5 years old), ChainSecurity explicitly flagged that deployed contracts deviate from the audited version (even if only cosmetically), no follow-up or differential audit from a recognized firm covering the 2022–2026 period was found, and no commit SHA could be pinned this run. The green case is undercut by audit staleness exceeding the 6-month rule; the red case is undercut by credible source-verification evidence from multiple search-result snippets and a recognized public repo.

evidence.shows: Polygon protocol website successfully fetched; confirms https://github.com/maticnetwork/ and https://github.com/0xPolygon as official GitHub orgs; links to docs.polygon.technology and forum.polygon.technology; confirms docs.polygon.technology/tools/security/ as security page.

protocol_metadata.about: Polygon Bridge (PoS Portal) is the canonical asset bridge connecting Ethereum (root chain) to the Polygon PoS network (child chain). Users deposit ERC-20, ERC-721, or ETH into predicate contracts on Ethereum, which lock assets while equivalent tokens are minted on Polygon; withdrawals require burning tokens on Polygon, waiting for a Heimdall checkpoint (≈30 min), then submitting a Merkle proof to the RootChainManager on Ethereum to unlock funds. The bridge uses an upgradeable proxy architecture (EIP-897 DelegateProxy) with a RootChainManager as the central coordinator and separate predicate contracts per token type.
